deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a wrapper or label sheet (cover slip) for a sub-file of the Gauss Nachlass, bundle Math. 21. It carries an archival shelfmark in pencil ('Math 21') and a folio number. The number '44' and a further number were struck through and replaced by '45'; separately, a circled '(44)' gives the current foliation. The handwritten title reads: 'Candidat Lieger zu Hoya (Berechnung der Ludolph'schen Zahl)', i.e. 'Candidate Lieger at Hoya (computation of Ludolph's number)'. 'Ludolph'sche Zahl' is the standard 19th-century German name for π, after Ludolph van Ceulen. 'Candidat' most likely means a candidate of theology or of school teaching. Hoya is a town on the Weser in the Kingdom of Hanover. The sheet therefore labels material sent to Gauss, presumably by an otherwise obscure correspondent, containing a computation of π. Such submissions reached Gauss in the 1840s, the period of Dase's 200-digit computation (1844) and Clausen's 250-digit computation (1847). The actual computation is not on this page and no previous or next page is supplied. No derivation can therefore be reconstructed or checked. The label may be in an archivist's hand (e.g. from the Nachlass ordering) rather than Gauss's own; this cannot be decided from the image alone.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is only a cover or label sheet with a title. It contains no mathematical content, only evidence that an amateur's π computation was filed among Gauss's papers.
transcription_corrections: The uncertain word '(Berechnung[?]' reads plausibly as 'Berechnung'; the question mark can probably be dropped.
'Ludolph'schen' may be written 'Ludolphi'schen' or with an apostrophe/accent mark over the final letters of 'Ludolph'; the meaning (π) is unaffected.

The surname read as 'Lieger' is plausible but not certain; the initial capital could also be read as 'R' (i.e. 'Rieger'). This should be verified against the correspondence catalogue of the Göttingen Gauss Nachlass.

The folio numbering is: '44' struck through, '45' written and then struck through, and the circled '(44)' is the current foliation. The transcription '[-44b-] [-45-] (44)' should read '[-44-] [-45-] (44)' if the first number is '44' rather than '44b'.
